extracted.intended_audience: journal editors/publishers and researchers considering adopting or using open science badges
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for journals and researchers on what Open Science Badges recognize, how they should be awarded and displayed, and what requirements underlie their validity (e.g., persistence and accessibility of shared materials).

rubrics_metrics.name: Badges acknowledge open science practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Badges to acknowledge open science practices are incentives for researchers to share data, materials, or to preregister.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open Science Badges enhance openness, a core value of scientific practice. Badges signal to the reader that the content has been made available and certify its accessibility in a persistent location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Badge types / What badges recognize
rubrics_metrics.description: Badges signal and reward when underlying data, materials, or preregistrations are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page repeatedly identifies three primary targets for badges: data, materials, and preregistration. Over 100 journals offer Open Science Badges to indicate availability of these underlying research artifacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awarding mechanism: disclosure vs independent review
rubrics_metrics.description: Each journal may choose to award badges based on a simple author disclosure statement or through independent peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals have discretion over whether to rely on authors' disclosure statements or to require independent verification/peer review before awarding a badge; the page explicitly lists both as acceptable approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display requirement: badge image plus disclosure statement
rubrics_metrics.description: As long as the badge image and disclosure statement are presented, you can display them any way you like.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The only display requirement specified is that both the badge image and its accompanying disclosure statement are present on the publication; journals may choose layout/format freely. The site provides downloadable badge images and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistence and accessibility requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Badges signal that the content has been made available and certify its accessibility in a persistent location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a badge to meaningfully indicate openness, the underlying materials/data/preregistration should be available in a persistent (archival) location so readers can access them over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visibility requirement for effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Badges must be visible on the table of contents and authors must be consistently asked to participate for badges to change community norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page cites evidence (Kidwell et al., 2016) that implementing badges is associated with increased data sharing, but emphasizes that badges must be visible (e.g., on the TOC) and that authors are consistently prompted to participate to produce norm change. Example implementations (Psychological Science) are provided as models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usage and attribution of badge images
rubrics_metrics.description: The badges are free to use with attribution of their source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Downloadable badge images are provided (link given). When using the badges, sites/journals should attribute the source as requested by the providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check for journal-specific/modified badge criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Some journals use modified badge criteria (e.g., BMC Microbiology 'uses modified badge criteria').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because some publishers or journals may alter the standard badge criteria, adopters and readers should consult individual journal policies or the published list (TOPFactor.org) to understand any deviations from the canonical badge definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence & rationale for adopting badges
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementing badges is associated with increasing rate of data sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page references empirical evidence (Kidwell et al., 2016) supporting badges as an incentive mechanism and points to real-journal examples to illustrate practical impact; adopters should consider this evidence when deciding to implement badges.
